title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 15-17 of this section of the notes). Grothendieck classifies 'additive invariants' of semi-simplicial sets and the 'operations' that act on them. Write Ss = Δ̂ for presheaves on Δ. Ab_* denotes simplicial (or cosimplicial, by duality) abelian groups and Ab_· denotes chain (or cochain) complexes. The two are related by DP, Dold-Puppe (Dold-Kan); ND on the next page is presumably the normalisation N.

(1) Invariants. A contravariant invariant with values in an additive category B is a functor F: Δ̂^op → B that turns colimits into limits. It is determined by its restriction to Δ, that is, by a cosimplicial object of B.

(2) Operations. An operation Ω is attached to an object L of Ab_* (equivalently of Ab_·). It acts on cosimplicial (resp. cochain) objects of any additive category with the relevant limits. In modern terms it is the weighted limit {L, Y}, an end ∫_n Hom(L_n, Y^n)-type construction.

The previous page records three points:
- Restricting the admissible value categories to those having only limits of a class L of index categories shrinks the universal category. One obtains the full subcategory U_L of (Ab_*)^op generated by the representables C_*(Δ^n) under L-limits.
- The top of this page closes that remark. For L = ∅ one gets the full subcategory of Ab_* generated by these objects under finite sums.
- This is exactly the theory of free completion under a class of (co)limits.

Remark c). Take B = Ab. Then the same objects, K_* ∈ Ab_* or K_· ∈ Ab_· at will, express two things:
- the lim-preserving contravariant invariants F: Δ̂^op → Ab;
- the operations Ω on contravariant or covariant invariants valued in an additive category with lim←.

If one takes K = L, how are F and Ω related? Answer: F is obtained by applying Ω to the universal invariant F_0: Δ̂^op → B_0 = (Ab_*)^op, X ↦ C_*(X)^op (free simplicial abelian group / chains). Hence
F(X_*) ≅ Ω^*_*(C_*(X_*)^op) ≅ Ω^·_·(C_·(X_*))^op.
Here C(X)^op is viewed as a cosimplicial (resp. cochain) object of B' = Ab^op, and Ω^*: B'^* → B' is evaluated in B = Ab^op.

This is the Yoneda/Kan-extension identification:
continuous F ↔ cosimplicial abelian groups ↔ continuous additive functors on Ab_*^op, with F(X) = Hom(Z[X], K) written as an end/weighted limit.

The bottom note warns about the variance: the F in question are contravariant with values in Ab, which amounts to working in (Ab)^op.

Grothendieck then states that all of this works for an arbitrary small category in place of Δ, and also in a non-additive context. What is specific is only the additive value categories and the Dold-Puppe equivalence.

He announces the real interest. These are the invariants coming from K_* ∈ Ab_* lying in U_L, i.e. describable by L-limits of the C^{[n]}_* = C_*(Δ^n), together with the analogous operations Ω_*. Next page: the role of DP, the multiplicative structures not matched by DP/N, and the tensor operations Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i being natural on Ab_*.

Purpose: a formal framework for producing cochain-type functors, such as a divided-power de Rham complex on simplices, as operations Ω applied to the universal chain functor C_*(X).
errors: Variance bookkeeping is slippery: the formula's two sides use (·)^op in different places, and Grothendieck himself adds a marginal 'Attention' about contravariance. The statement is correct modulo these conventions, but they are not spelled out on the page.

The characterisation of the operation category as U_L is asserted to follow from 'general principles (not detailed)'. It is not proved here, but it is correct as an instance of free completion under a class of limits.

ideas.what: Lim-preserving contravariant invariants Δ̂^op→Ab classified by (co)simplicial abelian groups, and recovered by applying the corresponding operation to the universal invariant X↦C_*(X)
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda/left Kan extension; weighted (co)limits; free cocompletion of Δ in additive setting (Ab_* as presheaves of abelian groups on Δ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (1958), Kelly 'Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory' (1982) for weighted limits
ideas.where_published: Similar Kan-extension reasoning pervades SGA4 (Exp. I) and Pursuing Stacks, but this specific formulation is not known to me in published texts

ideas.what: Category of operations commuting with limits of a prescribed class L equals the full subcategory U_L generated by representables under L-limits (L=∅: finite sums)
ideas.modern_name: Free completion under a class of limits / closure of a class of limits

ideas.what: Interchangeability of simplicial and chain descriptions (Ab_* vs Ab_·) via Dold–Puppe for both invariants and operations
Assertion that the formalism holds for any small category in place of Δ and in a non-additive context

missed.claim: Around 1976, before Kelly's 1982 book, Grothendieck sets up a theory in which operations on additive cohomology-type invariants are weighted limits indexed by simplicial abelian groups. Limiting the class L of limits available in the value categories yields smaller universal categories U_L, i.e. free completions under a class of limits. This anticipates the Kelly / Albert–Kelly 'closure of a class of limits' formalism and applies it to cochain theories on simplicial sets.
missed.quote: on s'intéressera surtout aux inv. contravariants en X_* provenant d'objets K_*∈Ab_* qui sont des U_L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of minor historical interest as an independent early use of weighted-limit/free-completion ideas. The ideas themselves are now standard, so the novelty is priority-type rather than mathematical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is foundational bookkeeping: Yoneda/Kan extension, weighted limits indexed by simplicial abelian groups, and Dold–Kan. All of this is standard today, though the free-completion-under-class-L viewpoint slightly predates its standard enriched-category formulation. Nothing on this page itself is a new result. The interesting divided-power de Rham content lies elsewhere in the dossier.
transcription_corrections: Top lines likely read: '(c'est ce qu'on a vu ci-dessus ... des catégories ... remarquables, y.c. celui où L=∅ et où on trouve la catégorie pleine de Ab_* engendrée par les C^[n]_* par sommes finies'.
'pour exprimer les effets contravariants F possibles' is more plausibly 'pour exprimer les invariants contravariants F possibles'.

'les Ψ {+Ω+} qui sont...' : the underlined symbol is likely the abbreviation 'op.' (opérations) with Ω written above, i.e. 'les op. Ω qu'on peut faire sur des inv. contravariants ou covariants à valeurs dans une cat. additive où existent les lim←'.
'une catégorie Δ (ou plutôt) quelconque' is more likely 'une catégorie Δ (ou petite) quelconque', i.e. any small category.
'C^{[n]}_*' denotes C_*(Δ^n), the free simplicial abelian group on the standard n-simplex.
